faq.a: There is no single Surrey farm belt in the sources used here: the live surrey-farms feed's three listings at reading sat in Sullivan Station (two, on the Colebrook side) and Fleetwood Tynehead (one), and the page's own related links point to Cloverdale Farms, South Surrey Farms and Port Kells Acreages as separate pockets.

faq.q: Can I Airbnb a Surrey farm house?
faq.a: Not as a whole-house rental by right: in the ALR, renting out the entire principal residence for short-term stays is not permitted outright and requires ALC approval, and the City of Surrey separately requires the host to be an owner living at the property as their primary residence, with a $358-per-year business licence.

faq.q: What is the ALR and does it apply to farms in Surrey?
faq.a: The Agricultural Land Reserve is farmland protected by the provincial Agricultural Land Commission. Farm use is generally allowed on ALR land, but subdividing, adding homes or using the land for non-farm purposes usually needs approval, so check a property's ALR status before you offer.

faq.q: What should I check before buying a farm in Surrey?
faq.a: Check the ALR status, water source and licences, drainage and flood history, the buildings and any quota or production licences that do or do not transfer with the land. Poultry and egg production in BC are supply-managed, so a sale of the farm does not automatically include quota.
